results.title: Democratic midterm gains may fuel fresh trade uncertainty for Korea
results.content: Democratic gains in both chambers of the U.S. Congress in the midterm elections could expose Korea to fresh trade uncertainty, as experts warn that while such a shift would do little to curb U.S. President Donald Trump's tariff powers, it could complicate the implementation of Seoul's investment commitments and prompt him to intensify trade pressure. The $350 billion investment agreement between Seoul and Washington is unlikely to be overturned, as expanding U.S. manufacturing has bipartisan support. However, the political fallout from the Republican defeat could put pressure on Trump to demonstrate progress on his trade agenda, with Korea potentially facing renewed tariff threats, the experts said. "The tools used to exert tariff pressure are unlikely to change," said Jang Sang-sik, head of trade trend analysis at the Korea International Trade Association, referring to Section 232 and S

results.title: Korean won to strengthen against dollar following Democrats' midterm sweep
results.content: The Korean won is expected to strengthen against the U.S. dollar after Democrats swept both chambers of Congress in the U.S. midterm elections, as political tensions in Washington and a potential sell-off in U.S. equities could weigh on the dollar, experts said Wednesday. Democratic control of Congress is expected to complicate U.S. President Donald Trump's efforts to advance his economic agenda, including tax cuts and expanded government spending, while giving lawmakers greater power to scrutinize his administration's policies. The prospect of a prolonged standoff between the White House and Congress could unsettle investors and undermine confidence in U.S. financial markets, said Shin Se-don, an economics professor at Sookmyung Women's University. "A fierce confrontation between Congress and the Trump administration will be inevitable. Trump's economic policy initiatives could face set

results.title: Imported vehicle sales jump 29.3% in Oct. on strong EV demand
results.content: Sales of imported vehicles in Korea rose a sharp 29.3 percent in October from a year earlier, driven by robust demand for electric vehicles (EVs), industry data showed Wednesday. New registrations increased to 31,117 units last month from 24,064 a year earlier, according to the Korea Automobile Importers & Distributors Association (KAIDA). The three top-selling imported cars were the Tesla Model Y Premium, Mercedes-Benz E200 and Tesla Model 3. The two Tesla models are manufactured in China for the Korean market, allowing the company to offer them at competitive prices. Tesla's sales more than doubled to 9,165 units last month from 4,350 a year earlier. However, its sales fell 25.9 percent from the previous month due to supply shortages, KAIDA said. The U.S. EV maker remained the best-selling imported passenger car brand in Korea for the ninth consecutive month, extending its run since Fe

results.title: Joint registration of taekwondo in order
results.content: South Korea, which globally popularized the martial art form of taekwondo, is waking up to find North Korea has already moved to register the sport on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage List. A technical advisory body is soon expected to recommend registration of "Taekwon-Do, traditional martial art in the Democratic People's Republic of Korea" for North Korea's solo application, submitted in March 2024. The final decision will be made in Xiamen, China, at the meeting of the Intergovernmental Committee for the Safeguarding of Intangible Cultural Heritage, scheduled for Nov. 30 to Dec. 5. If finalized, Seoul may be left scrambling to register taekwondo on its own. It does not have to be that way. The martial art has shared roots that predate the division of the two Koreas. results.title: Police arrest 80 high-risk offenders in relationship-based crime review
results.content: Police said Wednesday they have conducted a comprehensive review of about 44,000 cases involving relationship-based crime, such as stalking and domestic violence, and placed under custody 80 individuals identified as high-risk offenders. The 12-day review, which began Oct. 19, covered 44,540 cases, according to the Korean National Police Agency. They included 43,712 existing cases, such as those currently under investigation, individuals subject to high-risk monitoring, stalking reports that had previously been closed at the scene and cases involving ongoing safety measures. The police classified 5,068, or 32 percent, of the 15,840 cases currently under investigation as high-risk. Regarding high-risk offenders, police requested 376 arrest warrants, of which 80, or 21.3 percent, were issued by courts. They also requested 321 orders for the attachment of electronic monitoring devices, of w

results.title: More productive, attractive regions outside Seoul key to sustaining growth: OECD officials
results.content: Korea needs to boost productivity in regions outside the capital area and make them more attractive places to live as it seeks to sustain economic growth and address demographic challenges, officials at the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) said Wednesday. Lamia Kamal-Chaoui, director of the Center for Entrepreneurship, SMEs, Regions and Cities at the Paris-based institution, said in an interview with Yonhap News Agency that the OECD has seen "something very interesting" in Korea. Despite the concentration of people and economic activity in the capital region, the country's regional gaps in GDP per capita are among the smallest in the OECD, she said. "Indeed, you have the largest concentration of the capital region across the OECD," Kamal-Chaoui said. results.title: HS Hyosung vice chair highlights private diplomacy at OECD anniversary dinner
results.content: HS Hyosung Vice Chairman Cho Hyun-sang has stepped up efforts to promote private-sector diplomacy as Korea marks the 30th anniversary of its membership in the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD). Cho delivered congratulatory remarks at a dinner commemorating the anniversary, hosted by the Federation of Korean Industries (FKI) in Seoul Tuesday. He attended as a Korean board member of Business at OECD (BIAC). The event brought together around 80 participants, including OECD Deputy Secretary-General Frantisek Ruzicka, diplomatic representatives from 26 countries and Korean business leaders. They reviewed Korea's economic achievements over the past three decades and discussed ways to expand global economic cooperation. results.title: Seoul's outdoor libraries top 10 mil. visitors, set to reopen in April
results.content: d Seoul's outdoor libraries have drawn more than 10 million visits since their launch in 2022, turning public squares and urban waterways into popular reading spaces and drawing growing attention from overseas media and library professionals. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Wednesday that this year's program attracted approximately 1.87 million visitors to three main locations — Seoul Plaza, Gwanghwamun Square and Cheonggye Stream — before closing for its winter break on Nov. 1. The cumulative figure of more than 10 million includes visitors to district-run and pop-up outdoor libraries since the initiative began. A satisfaction survey of 5,155 visitors found that 97 percent were satisfied with the program, while 97.4 percent said they intended to return and 97.8 percent said they would recommend it to others. results.title: Seven Luck casino introduces 24-hour AI phone service in 4 languages
results.content: State-run casino operator Grand Korea Leisure (GKL) has introduced a 24-hour artificial intelligence (AI) telephone service at its Gangnam Coex branch, offering automated support in four languages — Korean, English, Chinese and Japanese — to streamline customer inquiries. The state-run casino operator said the AI call bot is the first system of its kind introduced in the industry and is designed to handle routine inquiries around the clock. Customers calling the branch can listen to an introductory message before asking questions in Korean or one of the three foreign languages, with the system responding in the language used. The AI service provides information about the casino's location, operating hours, parking facilities and admission requirements. Calls involving reservation checks or more detailed consultations are transferred to the appropriate staff members. GKL said it built a d

results.title: BMW Korea unveils facelifted 7 Series luxury sedan to take on Mercedes-Benz S-Class
results.content: BMW Korea unveiled its redesigned 7 Series luxury sedan, Wednesday, seeking to build on its growing presence in the higher-end market, as the flagship model gains ground rapidly against the long-dominant Mercedes-Benz Korea’s S-Class. The launch carries significance beyond the arrival of an updated model. The 7 Series has emerged as one of BMW Korea's key growth drivers, capitalizing on weakening demand for its archrival Mercedes-Benz S-Class in the large luxury sedan segment that BMW has traditionally struggled to dominate. The changing sales balance between the two models illustrates the shift. According to data from the Korea Automobile Importers & Distributors Association (KAIDA), the S-Class recorded 1,839 sales in Korea during the first half of this year, 1,238 fewer than the 7 Series' 3,077. The BMW luxury sedan also topped sales of imported large sedans in Korea in both 2024 and

results.title: Winter delicacy returns to Korea as plunging Pacific catch drives up prices
results.content: As the first crisp autumn winds sweep across the East Sea, the port city of Pohang in North Gyeongsang Province begins producing "gwamegi" — Korea’s cherished winter delicacy of dried Pacific saury. But this season, a sharp slump in oceanic catches is turning the savory staple into a luxury commodity. Pohang launched a nationwide promotional blitz on Wednesday at the National Assembly in Seoul, introducing the 2026–2027 season. Celebrated for its rich, chewy texture and deeply savory flavor, gwamegi is traditionally crafted in the seaside town of Guryongpo by hanging cleaned saury on wooden racks, allowing the freezing night temperatures and icy coastal winds to slowly dry and cure the fish over several weeks. results.title: Korea, African Union discuss cooperation fund, broader ties
results.content: Korea and the African Union (AU) have discussed ways to manage their joint cooperation fund and expand economic, healthcare and other forms of cooperation, Seoul's foreign ministry said Wednesday. The discussions took place during the seventh round of policy consultations in Addis Ababa on Tuesday (local time), with Chung Kwang-yong, director-general for African and Middle Eastern affairs at the ministry, and Willy Nyamitwe, chairperson of the AU's Permanent Representatives Committee, leading their delegations, according to the ministry. Established in 2002, the 54-member AU aims to promote African integration, peace and security. During the meeting, the two sides discussed ways to manage the Korea-AU Cooperation Fund and expand substantive cooperation in trade, investment, healthcare, youth and women's empowerment, climate change and peace and security, among other fields. results.title: Appeals court upholds Yoon's election law conviction, putting PPP funds at risk
results.content: An appellate court on Wednesday upheld the conviction of former President Yoon Suk Yeol for making false statements during his 2022 presidential campaign, a ruling that, if finalized, would require the main opposition People Power Party (PPP) to repay 39.7 billion won ($30 million) in campaign reimbursements. The Seoul High Court upheld a lower court’s sentence of 18 months in prison, suspended for three years, over statements Yoon made before his election in March 2022. The decision leaves the PPP facing a substantial financial liability, although the repayment obligation depends on the conviction becoming final at the Supreme Court. Under the election law, the government fully reimburses campaign expenses for political parties whose presidential candidates receive at least 15 percent of the vote. results.title: Coupang's mounting losses threaten growth model amid regulatory pressure
results.content: Coupang Inc., the U.S.-based operator of Korea's largest e-commerce platform, accumulated 1.83 trillion won ($1.28 billion) in operating losses in the first nine months of this year, as a data breach and regulatory pressure weigh on profitability. According to results released Wednesday, Coupang posted an operating loss of 642.3 billion won in the third quarter, following losses of 835 billion won in the second quarter and 354.5 billion won in the first quarter. The third-quarter loss included 354 billion won in expenses related to a July fire at its Incheon fulfillment center. The company also continued to bear costs from customer compensation following last year's data breach. A 624.7 billion won Fair Trade Commission (FTC) fine weighed on second-quarter earnings. The accumulated losses have nearly erased the 1.9 trillion won in operating profits Coupang generated between 2023 and 2025

results.title: Seoul forum to examine how personal taste turns into big business
results.content: The Seoul Design Foundation will hold a forum next week on how personal taste and shifting consumer values can be turned into brands and businesses. Entrepreneurs and creators from space design, fashion, publishing and food will speak. The Seoul Design Learn Forum 2026 runs from 2 p.m. to 6:10 p.m. on Tuesday in the Design Hall of Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), the foundation said Wednesday. DDP is a landmark complex in central Seoul designed by the late architect Zaha Hadid. Seoul Design Learn is a training program for people who want to start design businesses, offering hands-on classes, mentoring and networking. It applies the ideas behind Seoul Learn, the city’s main education platform, to design. results.title: Sunken treasures reveal secrets of Goryeo Korean maritime route
results.content: Off the rugged, wave-swept coast of Taean, a treacherous marine graveyard known historically as the "Racecourse of the Sea" has yielded two newly discovered Goryeo Dynasty shipwrecks, offering an unprecedented window into 13th-century statecraft, commerce and seafaring. The National Research Institute of Maritime Cultural Heritage said Wednesday that underwater archaeologists have fully identified the wreckage of the Mado No. 5 ship and spotted the traces of a brand-new wreck, Mado No. 6, nearby. Together, the finds illuminate the sophisticated tax-grain shipping networks that once fed the Goryeo capital of Gaegyeong. The excavation of the Mado No. 5 vessel recovered 54 artifacts, including bronze vessels, rope, anchors and bundles of preserved rice straw. results.title: Korea certifies its 1st official braille teachers century after invention
results.content: Exactly a century after the creation of Korean braille, Korea has certified its first cohort of 20 officially licensed braille instructors — a major step toward expanding educational accessibility for the visually impaired. The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism said Wednesday that the milestone fulfills a core mandate of the nation’s landmark Braille Act, passed a decade ago to formalize and elevate braille literacy across the country. The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and the National Institute of Korean Language said the 20 teachers received second-grade braille teacher licenses. The license is a national qualification created when the Braille Act was revised, and the change took effect last year. The announcement fell on Hangeul Braille Day, which was marked Wednesday. results.title: Jamsu Bridge car-free festival draws record crowds before pedestrian-only conversion
results.content: Seoul’s car-free festival on Jamsu Bridge drew a record 2.38 million visitors this year, the city said Wednesday. That brings attendance over five years to 7.68 million as the bridge gets ready to become a pedestrian-only crossing. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said this year’s Car-free Jamsu Bridge Ttubeok-ttubeok Festival ended on Oct. 25. “Ttubeok-ttubeok” is a Korean word for the sound of footsteps. Jamsu Bridge opened in 1976. It sits just above the Han River’s surface, under the upper deck of Banpo Bridge, making it the bridge closest to the water. Cars have been kept off it on festival Sundays since 2022. This year’s festival ran on 15 Sundays from April to June and from September to October, drawing an average of 159,000 visitors a day. results.title: Science ministry, AMD hold 1st steering meeting on AI chip partnership
results.content: The science ministry and U.S. chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) held the first steering committee meeting of their artificial intelligence (AI) chip partnership on Wednesday. AMD also hosted its flagship AI event in Korea for the first time. The meeting was held at the Westin Seoul Parnas hotel during AMD Advancing AI World Tour Seoul 2026, the Ministry of Science and ICT said. The two sides set up the committee to check, on a regular basis, how the memorandum of understanding (MOU) they signed in July is being carried out. Lee Do-gyu, head of the ministry’s Office of ICT Policy, met with Keith Strier, AMD’s senior vice president for global AI markets. They reviewed progress on the deal’s key tasks. results.title: Early risers get rare chance to walk across Jamsil Bridge at sunrise
results.content: Seoul residents and visitors will have a rare opportunity to cross one of the city's busiest vehicular bridges on foot at sunrise this month, as the capital expands a popular weekend fitness initiative designed to encourage a more relaxed lifestyle. The Seoul Metropolitan Government announced Wednesday that it will host its "Swieom-Swieom Morning" event on Jamsil Bridge from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m. on two upcoming Sundays, Nov. 8 and Nov. 22. The program takes its name from the Korean descriptive phrase "swieom-swieom," an expression that loosely translates to "taking it easy," "taking frequent breaks," or "moving at a gentle, unhurried pace." In a fast-paced metropolis famous for its high-stress palli-palli ("hurry-hurry") culture, the event aims to offer urbanites a slow-paced weekend routine. results.title: Seoul to curb downtown marathons after road closures disrupt 190 bus routes
results.content: Seoul plans to tighten oversight of downtown marathons through a joint consultative body with police and other government agencies, responding to mounting complaints about road closures, traffic congestion, noise and litter. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Wednesday it will work with city police authorities to review race schedules, routes, traffic diversions and safety management plans for 2027. Detailed arrangements will be announced in December. Organizers preparing next year’s events were asked to refrain from recruiting participants until consultations on safety plans and traffic restrictions are complete. “While we recognize the contribution marathons make to the health of many residents, the disruption caused by downtown races has recently become a growing concern for others,” said Cho Sung-ho, director general of the city’s tourism and sports bureau. “We ask event organize

results.title: APR's Medicube enters Canada's largest drugstore chain
results.content: Korean beauty company APR said Wednesday that its skin care brand Medicube is now being sold at all Shoppers Drug Mart stores, which is Canada’s largest drugstore chain. The move widens Medicube’s reach in North America. The launch was completed last month at all of the chain’s roughly 1,300 stores across Canada, including those in Toronto and Vancouver. Shoppers Drug Mart is a key subsidiary of Loblaw, one of Canada’s largest retailers. It began as a small pharmacy in 1920 and now sells medicine, cosmetics, skin care and household goods. Medicube offers 13 products at the chain. They include popular items already sold in North America, such as its Zero Pore Pad, PDRN Pink Peptide Ampoule, PDRN Pink Collagen Gel Mask and Deep Vita C Capsule Cream. results.title: Hyundai Motor Group faces lasting US policy risks after midterms
results.content: Hyundai Motor Group's massive investment in the United States could leave it with less leverage in future trade negotiations, as Washington's push to revive domestic manufacturing is expected to continue regardless of the outcome of the Tuesday (local time) U.S. midterm elections, a trade expert said in an interview on Wednesday. The automaker is increasingly vulnerable to changes in U.S. tariff and trade policies, particularly with its factories and supply chains fully established there, as political pressure on Korean manufacturers is likely to persist under either Republican or Democratic control of Congress, according to Shin Won-kyu, head of the global economic research team at the Federation of Korean Industries (FKI). results.title: Late baseball pitcher Choi Dong-won honored as Korean 'Sports Hero'
results.content: Choi Dong-won, widely considered one of the finest pitchers in Korean baseball history, was honored as the latest national "Sports Hero" on Wednesday. The Korean Sport & Olympic Committee (KSOC) named Choi, who passed away in 2011 at age 53, as the next inductee into its Sports Hall of Fame. The KSOC has been selecting one Sports Hero each year since 2011 to celebrate athletic feats of the country's sports stars. Choi is the first former baseball player to be so honored. Among the former athletes Choi joins are the 1936 Olympic marathon gold medalist Sohn Kee-chung, ex-International Olympic Committee Vice President Kim Un-yong, the 2010 Olympic figure skating champion Kim Yu-na and football legend Cha Bum-kun. results.title: Seoul Botanic Park opens giant greenhouse after dark with live music
results.content: Step out of the winter chill and into a glowing tropical sanctuary as Seoul Botanic Park opens its massive glass greenhouse for rare nighttime visits. Running across 10 select evenings from Nov. 13 to Dec. 27 at 6:30 to 8:30 p.m., the Night Botanic Journey transforms the indoor botanical garden — located in Gangseo District's Magok area in western Seoul — into an after-hours retreat featuring soft illumination, lush greenery and live musical performances ranging from jazz to classical concerts. The opening weekend, Nov. 13-14, will feature Jazz Libre and a musical gala under the theme "Greenhouse at Night, Two Sensibilities Meet." Pearl Haze and Mood Lamp Acoustic will perform Nov. 27 and 28, followed by vocalist duo Jang Ji-woong and Baek Seung-cheol and Ensemble Arang on Dec. 11 and 12. results.title: Seoul and Basel deepen architectural ties through international exchange
results.content: Seoul and Basel are looking to turn architectural dialogue into practical cooperation, bringing emerging Korean architects together with Swiss counterparts to exchange ideas on how cities can preserve their identities while adapting to changing social needs. Seoul's Deputy Mayor for Administrative Affairs Kim Seong-bo met with Conradin Cramer, head of the government of Basel-Stadt, in Basel on Nov. 3 to discuss cooperation in urban planning and architecture. The meeting followed an agreement on exchanges in urban architecture signed by Seoul and Basel-Stadt last year, with both sides reviewing their 2026 architect exchange program and exploring potential cooperation for the sixth Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism in 2027. results.title: SGI announces quarterly dividend for 2 consecutive quarters
results.content: Seoul Guarantee Insurance (SGI) said Wednesday that it has decided on a quarterly dividend of 573 won ($0.42) in cash per common share. The dividend per share is set at approximately 1.3 percent of the stock price, with the total dividend payout amount of about 40 billion won. The record date for the dividend is Nov. 18 and the payment date is scheduled for Dec. 2. Following a dividend payout of 30 billion won in the previous quarter, SGI confirmed a quarterly cash dividend for the second consecutive quarter. In August, the company unveiled its "corporate value enhancement plan and implementation status for 2026," setting a target of over 200 billion won in shareholder returns for this year — representing a shareholder return ratio of at least 50 percent — and became the first in the industry to implement quarterly dividends. results.title: Seo Yea-ji to return to big screen after 5 years with 'Geumwoldo'
results.content: Actress Seo Yea-ji is set to return to the big screen after five years with the upcoming film "Geumwoldo," marking another step in her acting comeback following controversies surrounding her personal life. According to her agency, B.Wave Entertainment, on Wednesday, Seo has been cast as Kim Ji-hoo in "Geumwoldo," a mystery thriller inspired by an actual case of cannibalism recorded in the Annals of the Joseon Dynasty. Set on a remote Korean island within an isolated community, the film will explore an unusual genre concept described as a "Korean-style vampire" story. It will be directed by Baek Dong-hoon, known for the film "Le Grand Chef 2: Kimchi Battle." Seo will play Kim Ji-hoo, a woman who travels to the remote island of Geumwoldo after receiving a message from her mother. results.title: GR Korea policy forum in Seoul to address Korea-UK AI strategies
results.content: British and Korean policymakers, lawmakers and artificial intelligence (AI) experts will gather in Seoul on Thursday to examine how their countries can strengthen AI competitiveness and cooperate on national strategies as governments confront the policy challenges posed by rapidly advancing technology. GR Korea and the British Chamber of Commerce in Korea will co-host a breakfast briefing titled "Politics of AI Breakfast: AI and National Strategy with BCCK" on Thursday at Conrad Seoul. Participants will include British Ambassador to Korea Colin Crooks, National Assembly member Rep. Lee Jeong-heon of the Democratic Party of Korea, and a British parliamentary delegation led by Alicia Kearns. results.title: Navy stages maritime maneuver drills to hone operability
results.content: The Navy has launched maritime maneuver drills in waters off the country's eastern, western and southern coasts in a bid to hone its operational capabilities against various maritime threats, the armed service said Wednesday. The Republic of Korea Navy Task Fleet Command is taking part in the drills, which kicked off Sunday for a six-day run, involving nearly a dozen warships and other aircraft, according to the Navy. Deployed assets include the Navy's 8,200-ton Jeongjo the Great destroyer, the ROKS Yulgok Yi I destroyer, auxiliary ships, frigates, and patrol aircraft. During the drills, the Navy will train under simulated attack scenarios involving air defense combat, antisubmarine warfare and antisurface warfare, and conduct drills to detect and track ballistic missile launches.
